description: Per-fund facts that Form N-PORT does not carry: net and gross expense ratio, inception, the exchange-traded product's own start date, tracked index and stated mandate. Read from each fund's own SEC-FILED summary prospectus (Form 497K), registration statement (Form 485BPOS) or prospectus supplement (Form 497) and committed with a URL, the form and filing date, and the date read. An SEC filing is used in preference to a sponsor web page for the reason Experiments 008 and 009 gave: a filing has an accession number and a permanent archive, and a web page has neither. This file is an INPUT to the screen, not an output of it, and it contains no price, return or performance data of any kind.
relationship_to_exp_002_facts: Every fund Experiment 002 already recorded keeps that experiment's facts VERBATIM, flagged carried_from_exp_002, so a fee or a stated mandate cannot differ between the two audits for a fund they share. Two fields are additional: etf_inception_date, which for a converted fund is the date the ETF began and not the predecessor mutual fund's inception; and stated_objective, the fund's own sentence from which its mandate was assigned.
mandate_rule: The stated mandate is the fund's own name and principal investment objective, as filed, reduced to Experiment 002's frozen vocabulary by this ordered test, applied before any return was downloaded. (1) Reduce the objective to a single factor: the one of the map's factors it names -- value, growth, momentum, quality or profitability -- or, where it names more than one, the one it names FIRST. That tie-break is the rule Experiment 002's own map note states in words when it says a multifactor mandate is graded on HML 'because every multifactor product in this universe names value first in its own objective'. (2) If the objective also names a size segment, use the compound mandate where the map has one, and the plain factor mandate where it does not. (3) If it names no factor but declares itself multifactor, factor-rotation or multi-signal, use `multifactor`. (4) If it names no factor and only a size segment, use that size mandate. (5) If it targets low or minimum volatility, record `min_volatility`, which is deliberately absent from the map and fails mandate_in_map. (6) If its stated objective changed inside the window, record `mandate_changed`, which is likewise absent from the map. Every fund decided by the tie-break in (1) is listed in mandate_first_named_factor_funds.
mandate_change_policy: Experiment 002's policy, unchanged. A fund whose STATED OBJECTIVE OR MANDATE changed inside the observation window is given the reserved mandate 'mandate_changed', which is absent from the intended-factor map and therefore fails the screen. It is recorded with its change date rather than silently dropped, because it has no single mandate over the window and so nothing to grade its exposure against. A change of tracked index, index name or methodology that leaves the stated mandate intact does NOT exclude a fund.

mandate_changes.change: iShares MSCI USA Multifactor ETF became iShares U.S. Equity Factor ETF; the index changed from an MSCI Diversified Multiple-Factor index to a STOXX Equity Factor index, whose quality score incorporates carbon-intensity and greenhouse-gas-target signals.
mandate_changes.why_tier_1: Experiment 002 classified this exact change, for INTF, as TIER 1 on the ground that the STOXX quality score uses signals the MSCI index did not, so the strategy changed in kind and not only in supplier. Experiment 009 carried that classification over to INTF, ISCF and EMGF for comparability. The same classification is carried over here for the two US members of the same transition. Grading one fund one way in the ex-US audit and another way here would be the discretionary edit these carry-overs exist to prevent.

mandate_changes.change: iShares MSCI USA Small-Cap Multifactor ETF became iShares U.S. Small-Cap Equity Factor ETF, on the same MSCI-to-STOXX transition. Its own performance table labels the benchmark 'STOXX U.S. Small-Cap Equity Factor Index (Spliced)', which is the fund recording the splice itself.
mandate_changes.why_tier_1: Same transition and same classification as LRGF.

gathering_note: Experiment 002's criterion order is preserved, so every criterion that can be evaluated from the census alone is applied before the two that need a filing. The set of funds requiring a prospectus read is therefore fixed by the census and not by how much looking was done, and a fund whose fee could not be verified FAILS maximum_expense_ratio and is recorded with that reason rather than quietly dropped.
